property.name: 325 Barrio
property.neighborhood: Logan Heights / Barrio Logan, San Diego, CA

places.name: Sawaya Brothers Market
places.blurb: Your closest option by far — a beloved neighborhood market just a block south on the same street, famous for fresh corn tortillas made on-site, a real carniceria (butcher counter), and Mexican grocery staples. Perfect for grabbing what you need to cook in without going anywhere.
places.address: 425 S 30th St Suite A, San Diego, CA 92113
places.hostTip: Go early for the warm corn tortillas — locals say they're worth the trip alone. Grab carne asada from the butcher and you've got dinner sorted.

places.name: Imperial Market
places.blurb: A friendly corner grocery a few blocks north on Imperial Ave, handy for cold drinks, snacks, and everyday essentials when you don't want to make a full grocery run. Quick neighborhood top-up spot.
places.hostTip: This is your late-evening backup for sodas, beer, or a forgotten ingredient — open till 10pm every night.

places.name: La Central Market
places.blurb: A longtime neighborhood institution (since 1970) over near Chicano Park, combining a grocery and liquor store with a made-to-order kitchen turning out fresh-dough pizza and tacos. A fun stop to pair with a stroll to the murals.
places.hours: Mon-Thu 7:00 AM - 10:00 PM, Fri 7:00 AM - 11:00 PM, Sat 8:00 AM - 11:00 PM, Sun 8:00 AM - 10:00 PM
places.hostTip: It's an easy detour on your walk to Chicano Park — grab a fresh pizza or tacos here while you pick up groceries and beer.

places.name: Northgate Market
places.blurb: The big, full-service Mexican supermarket at Mercado del Barrio — everything you'd want for cooking in, with an excellent carniceria, huge produce section, fresh tortillas, bakery, and a tortilleria. The real grocery-run destination of the neighborhood.
places.hostTip: This is the spot for a proper weekly shop. Park easily in the Mercado del Barrio lot, and hit the food stalls (mariscos, taproom) in the same plaza while you're there.

places.name: Cardenas Markets
places.blurb: A well-stocked Latino supermarket a short drive east on National Ave, with a strong meat and seafood counter, ample produce, and a hot-food kitchen. A solid full-size alternative when you're already in the car.
places.distanceText: not a realistic walk / ~6 min drive
places.hours: Daily approx. 6:00 AM - 11:00 PM (call to confirm)
places.hostTip: This is a drive-to destination, not a walk. Call ahead at (619) 239-4709 to confirm hours if you're going late — their Friday meat specials are worth timing a trip around.

places.name: Tacos El Trompo
places.blurb: This bustling al pastor specialist carves pork straight off the rotating trompo, and the tacos are some of the best in the neighborhood. It's the closest serious taqueria with long hours, making it your easy any-time-of-day option.
places.address: 1879 Logan Ave, Suite C, San Diego, CA 92113
places.hostTip: Order the al pastor with extra grilled onions and pineapple, and grab a side of their salsas. Open until 10pm daily, so it's your go-to for a late, cheap, authentic dinner.

places.name: El Carrito
places.blurb: A beloved Mexican breakfast and lunch spot built into a restored 1930s streetcar, just off Chicano Park. The chilaquiles and machaca plates are a local rite of passage.
places.hostTip: Come for breakfast and order the chilaquiles plus a cafe de olla, the spiced traditional coffee. Weekends bring menudo with hand-pressed tortillas — it fills up late morning, so go early.

places.name: Las Cuatro Milpas
places.blurb: A 1933 Barrio Logan institution famous for handmade tortillas, rolled tacos, and chorizo and beans, now reopened in a fresh space at Mercado del Barrio. The line moves fast and the food is the real, unfussy deal.
places.address: 1985 National Ave, Suite 1131, San Diego, CA 92113
places.hostTip: This icon reopened in May 2026 at its new National Ave home inside Mercado del Barrio. Go before noon to beat the line, grab a dozen warm tortillas to go, and don't skip the chorizo and beans.

places.name: La Fachada
places.blurb: A no-frills, family-run taco shop slinging carne asada, adobada, and seafood from early morning into the small hours. Locals swear it's the move after a night out.
places.hostTip: Open until 2-3am — this is your late-night hunger fix. The carne asada and adobada tacos are the classics, but the shrimp tacos hold their own too.

places.name: Fonda del Barrio
places.blurb: A popular sit-down Mexican spot on the Logan Ave corridor serving elevated regional dishes and classic antojitos in a lively, colorful room. A great choice when you want a fuller meal with table service in the mural district.
places.hostTip: A solid full-service option right in the heart of the Logan Ave scene. Confirm hours on their Instagram before walking over, as small barrio kitchens adjust schedules often.

places.name: Todo Pa' La Cruda
places.blurb: A well-known modern Mexican spot in the mural corridor known for hangover-cure comfort food, hearty plates, and creative takes on the classics. A fun, contemporary addition to the Logan Ave dining lineup.
places.hostTip: The name means roughly 'everything for the hangover,' so come hungry for the big breakfast and brunch plates. Mostly a daytime spot, so plan a morning or midday visit.

places.name: Ciccia Osteria
places.blurb: A Michelin Bib Gourmand Italian osteria set in a converted home, serving handmade pasta and Roman-style cooking. It's the neighborhood's special-occasion sit-down dinner.
places.hostTip: Reservations are strongly recommended and they're closed Tuesdays. The cacio e pepe and any handmade pasta of the day are the move. Small room, so book ahead.

places.name: El Rancho Tacos & Grill
places.blurb: A friendly sit-down taqueria and cantina on Logan Ave with both indoor and patio seating, plus a full menu of tacos, plates, and drinks. Easygoing spot to settle in for a meal.
places.hostTip: Grab the patio when the weather is nice and settle in with tacos and a margarita. A solid full-service option right in the mural corridor.

places.name: Las Ricas Tortas
places.blurb: A bright counter spot known for generously stacked tortas, fresh smoothies, aguas frescas, and fresas con crema. Great for a quick, satisfying, affordable lunch.
places.address: 1879 Logan Ave, Suite I, San Diego, CA 92113
places.hostTip: The tortas are huge, so one easily feeds you. Pair it with a mango or strawberry agua fresca. Shares a building with Tacos El Trompo, so you have options.

places.name: Northgate Market (Mercado del Barrio)
places.blurb: A large Mexican grocery with an excellent hot-food counter, tortilleria, and carnitas bar, plus a seating area. A budget-friendly way to eat well and stock the Airbnb at once.
places.hostTip: Hit the carnitas and prepared-food counter for an inexpensive feast, then grab fresh tortillas, fruit, and snacks for the rental on the same trip. Easy drive or a flat 20-minute walk.

places.name: Cafe Moto
places.blurb: A San Diego coffee institution since 1989, roasting fair-trade, organic, kosher beans in a solar-powered roastery right in the neighborhood. There's a drive-thru, a walk-up window, and street-side seats for your morning cup.
places.hostTip: This is your nearest real coffee, just down National Ave (the street one block south of the house). Grab beans here to brew back at the place — their single-origins from Mexico and Ethiopia are excellent.

places.name: Shepherds Coffee Co.
places.blurb: A thoughtfully designed specialty cafe at 25th & Imperial built to be a true 'third place' with Wi-Fi, outlets, and seating made for lingering. Handmade latte art and intentional, quality-first coffee.
places.hostTip: The best spot near the house if you want to post up and work for a couple hours. Head northwest on Imperial Ave to 25th. Note it's closed Sunday and Monday.

places.name: Por Vida
places.blurb: A vibrant Barrio Logan gem packed with local art, culture, and even a photo booth — more creative hangout than coffee counter. Their Mexican-inspired drinks, like the cinnamon-spiced horchata latte, are the move.
places.hostTip: Order the horchata latte and wander the Logan Ave mural strip right outside the door. Open every day and later than most, so it's your afternoon coffee fallback too.

places.name: Provecho Coffee
places.blurb: Specialty coffee tucked inside Bread & Salt, a converted 1950s bread factory turned art gallery, with a giant vintage bread mixer behind the bar. Sip an espresso tonic and wander the surrounding art installations.
places.hostTip: The owner's pick, and worth the walk. It's inside the Bread & Salt gallery, so make it a combined coffee-and-art outing. The cappuccino and espresso tonic are the standouts.

places.name: Drinky Promise
places.blurb: A cheerful, Latina-owned coffee spot on Logan Ave serving creative specialty drinks with a lot of heart. A warm, local neighborhood vibe that's become a Barrio Logan favorite.
places.hostTip: A friendly local pick right on the Logan Ave mural corridor, great paired with a stroll to Chicano Park. Closed Mondays, so plan around that.

places.name: Ryan Bros Coffee
places.blurb: The Barrio Logan home base and roastery of this longtime San Diego coffee family, with a full food menu and a deep bench of house-roasted espresso. A reliable, comfortable all-day cafe.
places.hostTip: Open until 5pm and serving real food, so it's your best bet when other neighborhood cafes have closed for the day. An easy detour if you're heading toward the waterfront or trolley.

places.name: The Shop Cafe Barrio Logan
places.blurb: A friendly, family-run cafe on Logan Ave with great specialty drinks and plenty of seating, from bar tables to stools. Easy parking in the back and a welcoming neighborhood feel.
places.hostTip: Strictly a morning spot (closes by 11am on weekdays), so catch it early. Worth driving to rather than walking given the distance west.

places.name: Mason Ale Works - Barrio Logan
places.blurb: Award-winning craft beer plus tacos in the heart of Barrio Logan's art-and-mural strip. This taproom recently revived the beloved old Border X Brewing space, so you get a fresh new spot with deep neighborhood roots, just a flat walk west from the house.
places.hostTip: Tuesdays are Taco Tuesday and they run Vinyl Nights and Padres/SDFC watch parties — check their Instagram (@masonaleworksbarriologan) before you head over so you can time a fun event.

places.name: Jaguar Paw
places.blurb: A cozy, candle-lit cocktail and natural-wine bar blending Mexican and Japanese flavors — think low-ABV cocktails, oysters, and rotating tostadas. Easily the most polished date-night drink spot in Barrio Logan, and a short walk from the house.
places.hostTip: It's small and gets busy on weekends — go early (right at 5pm) or be ready for a short wait. Ask the bartender to steer you to the right natural wine; the staff love doing it.

places.name: Tiny Giant Taproom
places.blurb: A laid-back, community-minded taproom with 30-plus ice-cold taps of San Diego and Baja beer, plus ciders, kombucha, and non-alcoholic pours. Quirky decor and a little arcade with pinball make it a fun, low-key hang inside the Mercado del Barrio.
places.address: 1985 National Ave, Ste 1132, San Diego, CA 92113
places.hostTip: There's a full menu of sandwiches and flatbreads plus NA beers, so it works even if not everyone in your group is drinking. Bring quarters for the pinball and the retro arcade.

places.name: Alchemy (Choose Thy Poison)
places.blurb: A frequently cited Barrio Logan drinks-and-food spot pouring creative cocktails alongside a solid kitchen. A fun, slightly eclectic option to round out a night in the neighborhood.
places.hostTip: A good cocktails-plus-food option in the mural corridor. Confirm current hours on their socials before walking over, as barrio spots adjust schedules seasonally.

places.name: Mujeres Brew House
places.blurb: San Diego's first Latina-owned, women-operated brewery and a true community hub a few blocks into the neighborhood. Bold, culturally inspired beers in a warm, welcoming taproom — a genuinely special stop worth supporting.
places.hours: Tue-Fri 4-10pm; Sat-Sun 12-9pm; Mon closed (alcohol service may be paused — verify before visiting)
places.hostTip: Heads up: Mujeres was navigating a 15-day alcohol-license suspension through June 4, 2026 — check their Instagram (@mujeresbrewhouse) or call before walking over to confirm they're serving beer.

places.name: Logan Inn
places.blurb: An unpretentious old-school neighborhood dive with a pool table, jukebox, and cheap, stiff pours. If you want the real, unvarnished Barrio Logan local-bar experience rather than a polished taproom, this is it.
places.hours: Wed-Mon roughly 10am-2am; Tue closed (call ahead to confirm)
places.hostTip: Bring cash — it's cash only and there may not be an ATM. This is a true dive, so come for the character and the pool table, not for craft cocktails.

places.name: Coronado Beach
places.blurb: Wide, soft, golden sand backed by the storybook Hotel del Coronado, this is regularly ranked among the best beaches in America. Astonishingly close to you, just over the bridge.
places.address: Ocean Blvd & Isabella Ave, Coronado, CA 92118
places.hostTip: Park free on Ocean Blvd if you arrive before 10am; otherwise the side streets near Star Park fill fast on weekends. The sand here actually sparkles thanks to trace mica.

places.name: Coronado Dog Beach
places.blurb: A relaxed, off-leash stretch of sand at the north end of Coronado Beach where dogs run free 24/7 with the Navy air station and bridge as a backdrop. A joy whether or not you bring a pup.
places.hostTip: Free dog waste bags and foot showers are right at the entrance to the run. Mornings are calmest before the crowds and the afternoon wind picks up.

places.name: Coronado Tidelands Park
places.blurb: The closest true waterfront to the house: a grassy bayfront park tucked right under the Coronado Bridge with calm-water beach, picnic lawns, and postcard skyline views back across the bay.
places.hostTip: This is the start of the flat Bayshore Bikeway and has the best up-close view of the bridge. Great for a sunset picnic with downtown lighting up across the water.

places.name: Embarcadero & Seaport Village
places.blurb: San Diego's downtown waterfront promenade: stroll past the USS Midway and tall ships, then browse the shops and waterside eateries of Seaport Village. An easy, breezy bayfront afternoon.
places.address: 849 W Harbor Dr, San Diego, CA 92101
places.hours: Seaport Village shops daily 10am to 9pm; waterfront promenade open 24 hours
places.hostTip: You can also reach downtown by the Orange Line trolley from 25th & Commercial (about a 10-12 min walk from the house), then walk over to the bay car-free.

places.name: Coronado Ferry Landing
places.blurb: Catch the harbor ferry across the bay to this charming Coronado waterfront village of shops and restaurants, with sweeping views of the downtown skyline. The boat ride is half the fun.
places.distanceText: not walkable / ~12 min drive to ferry, then 15 min crossing
places.hours: Ferry runs roughly hourly from San Diego, first ~9am, last departures 9-10pm; shops daily
places.hostTip: Drive to the Broadway Pier or 5th Ave Landing downtown and ride the ferry over (about $9 each way) rather than driving, so you skip Coronado parking entirely.

places.name: Silver Strand State Beach
places.blurb: A peaceful, family-friendly state beach on the narrow isthmus south of Coronado, with gentle surf on the ocean side and warm, calm water on the bay side. Less crowded than Coronado proper.
places.hostTip: Day-use parking runs about $10 (more on holiday weekends). Cross the highway via the underpass to the bay side if you want flat, kid-safe swimming.

places.name: Imperial Beach Pier & Portwood Pier Plaza
places.blurb: San Diego County's southernmost, most laid-back beach town: a long wooden fishing pier, 3+ miles of uncrowded white sand, and an unpolished, friendly surf-town vibe.
places.hours: Beach daily 6am to 10:30pm; pier daylight hours
places.hostTip: Mostly free street and lot parking, a rarity in San Diego. Check the water-quality posting before swimming, as the south end near the Tijuana River mouth can close after rains.

places.name: Sunset Cliffs Natural Park
places.blurb: Dramatic sandstone cliffs above the Pacific in Point Loma — the premier sunset-watching spot in the city. Wander the bluff-top trails as the sky goes orange over the water.
places.address: 1253 Sunset Cliffs Blvd, San Diego, CA 92107
places.hours: Daily, daylight hours (best ~30 min before sunset)
places.hostTip: Stay back from the crumbly cliff edges, especially at dusk. Arrive 30-40 minutes before sunset to snag the free lot near Ladera St and Cornish Dr.

places.name: Ocean Beach & Dog Beach
places.blurb: A bohemian, free-spirited beach town in Point Loma with a famous 24-hour off-leash dog beach, tide pools, and a funky main street of taco shops and antique stores a block back from the sand.
places.address: 5156 W Point Loma Blvd, San Diego, CA 92107
places.hostTip: The historic OB Pier is currently closed for replacement, so plan around the beach and the main-street scene rather than the pier. Sunsets here are excellent.

places.name: Mission Beach Boardwalk & Belmont Park
places.blurb: Classic Southern California boardwalk energy: a 3-mile beachfront path lined with rentals and snack stands, plus the vintage Giant Dipper wooden coaster at oceanfront Belmont Park.
places.hours: Belmont Park rides typically 11am to 8-10pm (varies by day/season); boardwalk open 24 hours
places.hostTip: Rent beach cruisers and pedal the flat boardwalk up toward Pacific Beach. Parking is tough on summer weekends, so come early or use the Belmont Park lot.

places.name: La Jolla Cove
places.blurb: A jewel-like cove ringed by cliffs where sea lions and seals haul out within feet of visitors and the clear water draws snorkelers and divers. The most scenic stretch of coast in San Diego.
places.hostTip: Go on a weekday morning for parking and calm water. By law you must keep your distance from the sea lions and seals, especially during spring/summer pupping season.

places.name: Chicano Park
places.blurb: The crown jewel of the neighborhood and a National Historic Landmark — this park beneath the Coronado Bridge holds the largest collection of outdoor Chicano murals in the world, painted across the bridge pylons. An unmissable, free, open-air gallery just a flat walk from your door.
places.address: 1949 Logan Ave (under Coronado Bridge), San Diego, CA 92113
places.hostTip: Head west on Imperial or Logan Ave and follow it toward the bridge. Go in morning light for the best mural photos, and look for spontaneous Aztec dancers on weekends.

places.name: Logan Avenue Mural Corridor
places.blurb: Beyond Chicano Park itself, the stretch of Logan Ave through the heart of Barrio Logan is lined with vibrant storefront murals, painted rolladens, and public art celebrating Chicano culture. A free, self-guided walk that pairs perfectly with the coffee shops and breweries along the way.
places.distanceText: 12 min walk / 4 min drive to the Logan Ave hub
places.address: Logan Ave between roughly 19th and 28th Sts, San Diego, CA 92113
places.hours: Open daily, daylight hours best for viewing
places.hostTip: This is distinct from the Chicano Park pylon murals — walk the Logan Ave storefronts between 19th and 28th to catch the gallery facades and painted security shutters, especially vivid when shops are closed and the rolladens are down.

places.name: Chicano Park Museum and Cultural Center
places.blurb: A bright, community-run museum at the edge of Chicano Park that adds context to the murals with rotating exhibitions on Chicano art, history, and activism. A perfect pairing right after you walk the park itself.
places.hostTip: Only open Thursday through Sunday, so plan around that. Admission is $8 general, and just $3 if you mention you're staying in the barrio.

places.name: Memorial Community Park & Bill and Maxine Wilson Skatepark
places.blurb: Your closest green space, literally a few blocks down 30th St. This neighborhood park has a 22,000 sq ft concrete skatepark, ballfields, picnic areas, and a pool — the historic heart of old Calle Treinta. Great for a quick stroll, a skate session, or letting kids burn energy.
places.address: Memorial Community Park, 30th St & Ocean View Blvd, San Diego, CA 92113
places.hours: Park daily roughly 6:00 AM - 10:00 PM; skatepark dawn to dusk
places.hostTip: Just walk south on 30th St — it's the closest open space to the house. Bring your own board and pads; the skatepark is free and unsupervised.

places.name: Bread & Salt (Athenaeum Art Center)
places.blurb: A sprawling former bread factory reborn as one of San Diego's most ambitious art spaces, with multiple galleries, the Athenaeum Art Center, print studios, and an affordable concert series. Raw industrial walls, serious contemporary art, and always something experimental on view.
places.hours: Tue-Sat 11:00 AM - 4:00 PM; extended 5-8 PM on 2nd Saturdays for the Art Crawl
places.hostTip: Free to wander the galleries. Check their site for a Fresh Sound concert during your stay — the acoustics in the old factory are something special.

places.name: Barrio Art Crawl
places.blurb: On the second Saturday of every month, Logan Ave comes alive as galleries throw open their doors, studios welcome visitors, live music spills onto sidewalks, and vendors line the street. The single best way to experience the barrio's creative scene all at once.
places.distanceText: 11 min walk / 4 min drive to the Logan Ave hub
places.address: Logan Ave between roughly 19th and 28th Sts, San Diego, CA 92113
places.hours: 2nd Saturday of each month, roughly 12:00 PM - 6:00 PM (galleries often run later)
places.hostTip: If your stay lands on a second Saturday, don't miss it. Walk west on Logan Ave — it's free, family-friendly, and the most fun the district sees all month.

places.name: Por Vida Coffee
places.blurb: An iconic Barrio Logan cafe wrapped in a hand-painted mural, with a tucked-away gallery in the back showcasing local artists. Equal parts great coffee and cultura — it makes a perfect first stop before exploring the murals.
places.hostTip: Grab a cafe de olla, then peek at the rotating art show in the back room. It's right on the mural corridor, so make it the launch point for your art walk.

places.name: Mercado del Barrio & Northgate Market
places.blurb: A lively mixed-use plaza under the Coronado Bridge anchored by the bustling Northgate Market, with a community stage, kids' fountain, public art, and a cluster of eateries and a taproom. Great for an authentic grocery wander, fresh tortillas, or a quick bite.
places.address: 1950 Main St (Mercado del Barrio), San Diego, CA 92113
places.hours: Market daily approx. 7:00 AM - 10:00 PM; plaza open daily
places.hostTip: Hit the Northgate hot-food counter and juice bar for an affordable, delicious lunch. It's a long but flat walk, or a quick drive with easy parking.

places.name: Cesar Chavez Park
places.blurb: A waterfront park on San Diego Bay with a recreational fishing pier, big bay and Coronado Bridge views, and breezy green lawns. The spot to catch a sunrise or sunset and watch tugboats and Navy ships work the harbor.
places.address: 1449 Cesar E Chavez Pkwy, San Diego, CA 92113
places.hostTip: Best at golden hour for bridge and bay views. It's a bit far on foot through industrial blocks, so I'd drive — free parking is on site.

places.name: La Bodega Gallery & Studios
places.blurb: A 1917 former Bank of Italy warehouse turned art collective, home to dozens of working artist studios and a 1,600 sq ft gallery known for lively shows like the annual Dia de los Muertos skull exhibit. A cornerstone of the barrio's grassroots art scene.
places.hours: Typically Mon-Fri 12:00 PM - 5:00 PM and during the 2nd-Saturday Art Crawl (verify before visiting)
places.hostTip: Their website may be out of date — check their Instagram (@labodegagallery) or Facebook for current hours and openings before heading over, especially outside Art Crawl weekend.

places.name: 25th & Commercial Trolley Station (Orange Line)
places.blurb: Your handiest trolley stop — a flat ~12-minute walk northwest through the Logan Heights grid. Hop the Orange Line west and you're in downtown San Diego in minutes, or ride east toward El Cajon.
places.address: Commercial St & 25th St (Cesar E. Chavez Pkwy), San Diego, CA 92113
places.hours: Trolley runs roughly 5 AM-midnight daily; trains about every 15 min (15-30 min off-peak)
places.hostTip: Tap a contactless credit card or the PRONTO app right at the platform reader — no paper ticket needed. Fares cap at the day-pass rate, so you'll never overpay if you ride a few times in one day.

places.name: 32nd & Commercial Trolley Station (Orange Line)
places.blurb: The other Orange Line option, a short flat walk northeast of the house. Same line as 25th & Commercial, so pick whichever direction your day is heading.
places.address: 32nd St & Commercial St, San Diego, CA 92113
places.hours: Trolley runs roughly 5 AM-midnight daily; trains about every 15 min (15-30 min off-peak)
places.hostTip: This station sits a bit closer if you're walking from the east side of 30th St. Both 25th and 32nd are on the same Orange Line, so just catch whichever platform you reach first.

places.name: Barrio Logan Trolley Station (Blue Line)
places.blurb: Down by the waterfront near Chicano Park, this is the Blue Line stop that links you south to the border at San Ysidro and north up to downtown and beyond. A scenic ~20-minute stroll past the murals to get there.
places.hours: Trolley runs roughly 5 AM-1 AM daily; trains about every 15 min (Blue Line is the busiest line)
places.hostTip: Take the Blue Line all the way south to San Ysidro if you want to walk across to Tijuana — it's the end of the line. The walk over here also takes you right through Chicano Park's famous murals, so build in a few minutes to look up.

places.name: 12th & Imperial Transit Center (all-lines trolley hub)
places.blurb: The grand central of the San Diego Trolley, the only station served by every line: Blue, Orange, Green, and Silver. Too far to walk, but a quick rideshare or one stop on the trolley puts the whole system at your fingertips.
places.hours: Trolley runs roughly 5 AM-1 AM daily; major transfer hub with frequent service across all lines
places.hostTip: If you need to switch between trolley lines, this is the one spot where every line meets. It's also a half-block from Petco Park, so it's the stop for a Padres game.

places.name: MTS Route 11 / 4 Bus (Imperial & National Ave stops)
places.blurb: You don't have to walk far for the bus — MTS routes run along Imperial Ave one block north and National Ave one block south of the house. Handy for hopping toward downtown or the trolley without the full walk.
places.address: Imperial Ave & 30th St / National Ave & 30th St, San Diego, CA 92113
places.hours: MTS local buses generally run ~5 AM-11 PM daily; check the MTS app or PRONTO for real-time arrivals
places.hostTip: Download the free PRONTO or Transit app to see exactly which bus is coming and when — real-time arrivals beat guessing at the stop. Same $2.50 fare as the trolley with a free 2-hour transfer.

places.name: San Diego International Airport (SAN)
places.blurb: One of the most conveniently close airports in the country — SAN sits just about 6 miles northwest, hugging the bay. An easy rideshare for arrivals and departures.
places.address: 3225 N Harbor Dr, San Diego, CA 92101
places.hours: Airport open 24 hours; most terminal services run ~4 AM-midnight
places.hostTip: At ~6 miles a rideshare runs roughly 15 minutes outside rush hour. Lyft and Uber pick up at the designated airport rideshare zones — follow the signs after baggage claim rather than the curb out front.
